name: it.lazyanalysis/lazyanalysis
title: LazyAnalysis — AI Solution Composer
description: Compose downloadable graphs and dashboards with native, Formula, Python and reusable Super Nodes.

tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.description:
Start here for LazyAnalysis reactive graphs, dashboard authoring and publishing,
        themes, nested supernodes, and the actions this MCP server supports.
        Example: get_capabilities() first in a session, then get_guide().

tools.name: describe_deployment_bundle
tools.description:
Describe deployment.json schema 2 (recommended): applications with
        launch kind app/instance/studio, equipment_writes read-only/operator/
        automatic, restart policy and depends_on, plus services (private
        loopback MQTT broker, command services with readiness probes, TCP
        checks) and the local launcher (lazyanalysis --launch, File > Open
        deployment, systemd/Windows logon installers). Schema 1 is still
        described. This server cannot provision, execute deployments, access
        credentials or grant equipment writes.
        Example: describe_deployment_bundle() before writing a .lazydeploy for prepare_deployment_bundle.

tools.name: prepare_deployment_bundle
tools.description:
Validate a deployment description and return the whole kit as text.
        Schema 2: deployment.json, launch.sh, launch.ps1, install-service.sh,
        remove-service.sh, install-service.ps1, remove-service.ps1, broker
        reference config and README, with the start order and the applications
        whose automatic equipment writes need local consent. Schema 1: the
        original read-only instance manifest and wrappers. Does not read local
        paths, run scripts, install services or provision identities. Supply
        only relative graph paths; never credentials. equipment_writes is a
        request the local operator confirms, not an authorization.
        Example: prepare_deployment_bundle(document={"schema_version": 2, "name": "Cell", "services": [{"name": "broker", "kind": "mqtt-broker", "port": 1883}], "applications": [{"alias": "hmi", "graph": "hmi.lazy", "mode": "desktop", "equipment_writes": "operator", "depends_on": ["broker"]}]}).

document.description: The deployment description as a JSON object (schema 2: name, services, applications, optional machines and addresses). See describe_deployment_bundle.
document.title: Document

tools.name: describe_distributed_systems
tools.description:
How to build systems of several LazyAnalysis applications: one instance reading devices all over a
        network, several processes on one computer, edge PCs and servers on a private network, and edge,
        manager and boss hierarchies. Covers the links between applications (distributed MQTT, Sparkplug,
        HTTP, WebSocket, UDP, TCP, ROS), equipment writes, heartbeats and watchdogs, complete .lazydeploy
        examples (checked by the launcher) and the exact commands that launch a deployment or one application
        on a computer or edge PC, by hand or as a service. topic: topologies, links, writes, launching, steps,
        or an example (same_computer, plant_network, edge_manager_boss); empty for everything. Composing only:
        this server never starts, installs or authorizes anything.
        Example: describe_distributed_systems(topic="plant_network") for a complete multi-computer deployment, or topic="launching" for the commands.

topic.description: One part of the guide: topologies, links, writes, launching, steps, or an example name (same_computer, plant_network, edge_manager_boss). Empty returns everything.
topic.title: Topic

tools.name: describe_spatial_dashboard
tools.description:
Discover embedded images, normalized anchors, card connectors, routing, animation,
        wireless signal bindings, property ranges, native limitations and authoring example.
        Example: describe_spatial_dashboard() before adding an equipment picture with animated connectors to a dashboard spec.

tools.name: get_solution_pattern
tools.description:
Discover proven composition patterns. With pattern='nested_dashboard', return a complete
        spec showing a Graph supernode with its own dashboard, a Graph portal card on the parent
        dashboard, named input/output ports, and a parameter exposed through two graph levels.
        The native desktop application provides child-dashboard navigation and Back to parent/root
        controls in View mode. Customize after inspecting the current catalog, then create_graph.
        Example: get_solution_pattern(pattern="nested_dashboard").

pattern.description: The pattern to return, e.g. nested_dashboard. Empty lists the available patterns.
pattern.title: Pattern

tools.name: get_geospatial_capabilities
tools.description:
Maps and geographic data: coordinate systems (WGS84 and others), raster and elevation
        layers, spatial indexing, vector features and topology, editable zones and 3D terrain. With
        a workflow name, the exact nodes, pins, links and settings of that workflow. Results follow
        this server's native catalog; workflows whose nodes are missing are not offered as runnable.
        Does not execute the graph.
        Example: get_geospatial_capabilities(workflow="vector_gis").

workflow.description: A workflow name (e.g. coastal_raster, tiled_raster, indexed_features, vector_gis) for its pins, links and settings. Empty returns the overview.
workflow.title: Workflow

include_unavailable.description: Also list workflows whose nodes are missing from this server's catalog.
include_unavailable.title: Include Unavailable

tools.name: describe_industrial_capabilities
tools.description:
What LazyAnalysis offers for industrial applications, from the loaded native catalog, and the
        limits of each area. historian_and_alarms: recording and replay, timestamps, quality, alarms with
        operator controls, asset hierarchy, SCADA dashboards. security_and_delivery: authorization rules,
        audit and durable at-least-once delivery. digital_twin: models running beside a machine.
        condition_monitoring: vibration analysis and visual inspection. complete_solution: combining them
        in one graph and handing it to an edge supervisor. Read only: no equipment is touched.
        Example: describe_industrial_capabilities(area="condition_monitoring").

area.description: Which features: historian_and_alarms, security_and_delivery, digital_twin, condition_monitoring or complete_solution. Empty lists the areas.
area.title: Area

tools.name: inspect_telemetry_delivery_health
tools.description:
Classify the health of a durable telemetry outbox (backlog, delivery, audit and storage) from
        counters you supply: healthy, degraded or faulted, with the reasons. Does not read live
        equipment, secret stores or remote journals.
        Example: inspect_telemetry_delivery_health(snapshot={"pending": 12, "capacity": 1000, "delivered": 480, "attempted": 492, "failed": 0, "rejected": 0, "audit_failures": 0, "storage_errors": 0, "connected": true, "faulted": false, "recording": true}).

snapshot.description: Counters you supply as JSON: pending, capacity, delivered, attempted, failed, rejected, audit_failures, storage_errors, and the flags connected, faulted, recording. Nothing is read from equipment.
snapshot.title: Snapshot

tools.name: compose_industrial_solution
tools.description:
One graph spec combining a historian with alarms (scada), vibration monitoring (vibration),
        visual inspection (visual) and a digital twin (twin) for one asset, with its dashboards, built
        from validated native nodes. Advisory only: it never commands equipment. Next:
        review_industrial_solution, then create_graph.
        Example: compose_industrial_solution(requirements={"name": "Pump 3", "asset_path": "Plant/Line1/Pump3", "modules": ["scada", "vibration"]}).

requirements.description: What the solution needs: name, asset_path (e.g. Plant/Line1/Pump3), modules (any of twin, vibration, visual, scada) and the vibration parameters sample_rate_hz, shaft_rpm and window_size.
requirements.title: Requirements

tools.name: review_industrial_solution
tools.description:
Check an industrial graph spec before create_graph: only allowed node types, correct wiring,
        passive settings (no equipment writes) and a readable layout. Returns the problems to fix.
        Example: review_industrial_solution(spec=<the spec from compose_industrial_solution>).

spec.description: A graph spec (as returned by compose_industrial_solution or written by you) to check before create_graph.
spec.title: Spec

tools.name: prepare_edge_release_manifest
tools.description:
Bind the exact bytes of a .lazy file to an unsigned release manifest for a trusted edge
        supervisor at the site. Signing, staging, approval and running happen on that supervisor,
        never through this server.
        Example: prepare_edge_release_manifest(graph_file=<create_graph(..., include_file=true).graph_file>, site_id="plant-milan", release_id="line1-r7").

graph_file.description: The .lazy file content as a JSON object, exactly as create_graph returned it.
graph_file.title: Graph File

site_id.description: The site the release is for, e.g. plant-milan.
site_id.title: Site Id

release_id.description: Your identifier for this release, e.g. line1-r7.
release_id.title: Release Id

include_exact_json.description: Also return the canonical JSON bytes the manifest hashes.
include_exact_json.title: Include Exact Json

tools.name: compose_vibration_monitoring
tools.description:
A graph spec that monitors a rotating machine's vibration: waveform, spectrum, RMS, crest
        factor, learned baseline, alarms and a historian, with a dashboard. Starts on a simulated
        signal; replace the source with the real sensor node. Advisory only, no equipment output.
        Example: compose_vibration_monitoring(asset_path="Plant/Line1/Pump3", sample_rate_hz=2048, shaft_rpm=1480, alarm_rms=4.5).

asset_path.description: Asset hierarchy path of the monitored machine, e.g. Plant/Line/Pump.
asset_path.title: Asset Path

shaft_rpm.description: Shaft speed in revolutions per minute, used for the order (1x, 2x) bands.
shaft_rpm.title: Shaft Rpm

window_size.description: Samples per analysis window (a power of two is best for the FFT).
window_size.title: Window Size

alarm_rms.description: RMS vibration level that raises an alarm, in the signal's units.
alarm_rms.title: Alarm Rms

alarm_crest.description: Crest factor (peak / RMS) that raises an alarm.
alarm_crest.title: Alarm Crest

alarm_residual.description: Deviation from the learned baseline that raises an alarm.
alarm_residual.title: Alarm Residual

baseline_alpha.description: Smoothing factor of the baseline, 0 to 1 (smaller adapts more slowly).
baseline_alpha.title: Baseline Alpha

baseline_deviation.description: Allowed deviation from the baseline, in standard deviations.
baseline_deviation.title: Baseline Deviation

signal_amplitude.description: Amplitude of the simulated test signal the graph starts with.
signal_amplitude.title: Signal Amplitude

signal_frequency_hz.description: Frequency of the simulated test signal, in Hz.
signal_frequency_hz.title: Signal Frequency Hz

tools.name: analyze_vibration_samples
tools.description:
Analyze one window of vibration samples you supply: RMS, crest factor, kurtosis, order
        harmonics, residual against a model, alarms and possible fault hypotheses (not diagnoses).
        Never reads a live sensor.
        Example: analyze_vibration_samples(samples=[0.01, 0.42, -0.38, ...], sample_rate_hz=1024, shaft_rpm=1800).

samples.description: One window of vibration samples (numbers), supplied by you.
samples.title: Samples

model.description: Optional expected samples (same length) to compute the residual against.
model.title: Model

quality.description: Quality of the samples: good, uncertain or bad.
quality.title: Quality

sample_rate_hz.description: Sample rate of the samples, in Hz.
sample_rate_hz.title: Sample Rate Hz

shaft_rpm.description: Shaft speed in revolutions per minute.
shaft_rpm.title: Shaft Rpm

alarm_rms.description: RMS level that counts as an alarm.
alarm_rms.title: Alarm Rms

alarm_crest.description: Crest factor that counts as an alarm.
alarm_crest.title: Alarm Crest

alarm_residual.description: Residual against the model that counts as an alarm.
alarm_residual.title: Alarm Residual

tools.name: analyze_health_trend
tools.description:
The trend of a machine's health score over time from rows you supply: slope, when it would
        cross the warning level, and how strong the evidence is. Makes no remaining-useful-life
        promise it cannot support.
        Example: analyze_health_trend(rows=[{"timestamp_s": 0, "health": 0.95, "quality": "good"}, {"timestamp_s": 3600, "health": 0.9, "quality": "good"}, ...], warning=0.5).

rows.description: Health rows you supply, each {"timestamp_s": seconds, "health": 0 to 1, "quality": "good"}, oldest first (rows not good are skipped).
rows.title: Rows

warning.description: Health below which the trend is a warning, 0 to 1.
warning.title: Warning

min_points.description: Fewest rows needed before a trend is reported.
min_points.title: Min Points

tools.name: compose_visual_inspection
tools.description:
A graph spec that compares a camera image with a reference inside a region of interest and
        raises an alarm when too much of it changed (leaks, deposits, missing parts), with a dashboard.
        Starts on simulated images; replace them with the camera node. No equipment output.
        Example: compose_visual_inspection(width=64, height=48, roi=[8, 8, 32, 24]).

width.description: Width of the inspected image in pixels.
width.title: Width

height.description: Height of the inspected image in pixels.
height.title: Height

asset_path.description: Asset hierarchy path of the inspected equipment.
asset_path.title: Asset Path

baseline_value.description: Gray level (0 to 1) of the simulated reference image.
baseline_value.title: Baseline Value

current_value.description: Gray level (0 to 1) of the simulated current image.
current_value.title: Current Value

delta_threshold.description: Change in gray level (0 to 1) that marks a pixel as changed.
delta_threshold.title: Delta Threshold

affected_fraction_alarm.description: Fraction of changed pixels (0 to 1) that raises an alarm.
affected_fraction_alarm.title: Affected Fraction Alarm

roi.description: Region of interest [x, y, width, height] in pixels; omit for the whole image.
roi.title: Roi

tools.name: analyze_visual_change
tools.description:
Compare two grayscale images you supply inside a region of interest: how many pixels
        changed, by how much, and whether that is an alarm. No camera or equipment access.
        Example: analyze_visual_change(image=[[0.5, 0.6], [0.5, 0.9]], baseline=[[0.5, 0.5], [0.5, 0.5]]).

image.description: The current grayscale image you supply, rows of values from 0 to 1.
image.title: Image

baseline.description: The reference image, same size as image.
baseline.title: Baseline

roi.description: Region of interest [x, y, width, height] in pixels; omit for the whole image.
roi.title: Roi

delta_threshold.description: Change in gray level (0 to 1) that marks a pixel as changed.
delta_threshold.title: Delta Threshold

affected_fraction_alarm.description: Fraction of changed pixels (0 to 1) that raises an alarm.
affected_fraction_alarm.title: Affected Fraction Alarm

quality.description: Quality of the images: good, uncertain or bad.
quality.title: Quality

tools.name: compose_digital_twin
tools.description:
A graph spec with a first-order digital twin of a machine: it predicts what the machine
        should do, compares it with the measurement and shows the difference, with a dashboard. Use
        fit_first_order_model first to get tau_s and gain from a recorded step. Never drives equipment.
        Example: compose_digital_twin(asset_path="Plant/Line1/Oven", tau_s=45, gain=1.8, mode="shadow").

asset_path.description: Asset hierarchy path of the modelled equipment.
asset_path.title: Asset Path

source_value.description: Initial value of the simulated measured signal.
source_value.title: Source Value

timestamp_s.description: Start time of the simulation, in seconds.
timestamp_s.title: Timestamp S

mode.description: simulation (a simulated source) or shadow (follows a measured signal).
mode.title: Mode

tau_s.description: Time constant of the first-order model, in seconds.
tau_s.title: Tau S

alpha.description: Filter gain for the value correction, 0 to 1.
alpha.title: Alpha

beta.description: Filter gain for the rate correction, 0 to 1.
beta.title: Beta

max_gap_s.description: Longest gap between measurements, in seconds, before the twin reports stale.
max_gap_s.title: Max Gap S

tools.name: fit_first_order_model
tools.description:
Estimate the time constant, gain and dead time of a first-order model from a recorded step
        response you supply, with how well it fits. Feed the result to compose_digital_twin.
        Example: fit_first_order_model(samples=[{"timestamp_s": 0, "value": 20, "quality": "good"}, {"timestamp_s": 10, "value": 31, "quality": "good"}, ...], input_step=10).

samples.description: Step response rows you supply, each {"timestamp_s": seconds, "value": number, "quality": "good"}, oldest first.
samples.title: Samples

input_step.description: Size of the input step that produced the response.
input_step.title: Input Step

tools.name: compose_historian_dashboard
tools.description:
A graph spec with a simulated signal, a historian that records and replays it, an alarm with
        operator acknowledge, and the SCADA dashboard cards for both. Replace the source with the real
        device node. Next: create_graph, then validate_graph. Never starts recording or writes.
        Example: compose_historian_dashboard(name="Line 1 historian and alarms").

source_value.description: Value of the simulated numeric source the dashboard starts with.
source_value.title: Source Value

tools.name: validate_asset_hierarchy
tools.description:
Check a Plant/Line/Cell/Equipment/Signal hierarchy: paths, sources, units and duplicates.
        Keeps the good signals and lists the bad rows. No network, no rights, no writes.
        Example: validate_asset_hierarchy(document={"version": 1, "signals": [{"path": "Milan/Line1/Cell2/Pump3/Flow", "source": "flow_meter", "unit": "l/min"}]}).

document.description: The asset hierarchy as JSON: {"version": 1, "signals": [{"path": "Plant/Line/Cell/Equipment/Signal", "source": node or tag, "unit": optional}]}.
document.title: Document

tools.name: query_historian_samples
tools.description:
Filter and summarize historian rows you supply by tag and time, keeping quality. Does not
        open journals or act on equipment; the HistorianNode records and replays inside a graph.
        Example: query_historian_samples(samples=[{"tag": "flow", "source_time": 1764316800, "value": 12.5, "quality": 0}], tag="flow").

samples.description: Historian rows you supply, each {"tag", "source_time" (seconds), "value", "quality" (integer 0 to 255, 0 good)}.
samples.title: Samples

tag.description: Only rows of this tag; empty for every tag.
tag.title: Tag

since.description: Earliest time to include, in seconds (Unix time).
since.title: Since

until.description: Latest time to include, in seconds (Unix time).
until.title: Until

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description:
How LazyAnalysis graphs work and how to describe one for create_graph. Read it first.
        Example: get_guide() once, before the first create_graph.

tools.name: read_help
tools.description:
The help of LazyAnalysis (what people see with F1): what the platform is for and how it works,
        the node editor, dashboards and how cards react to the graph, supernodes and their parameters,
        Theme Studio, the Python node, sharing, AI assistants and the example graphs. Without a page:
        the list of pages. With a page id (e.g. "how_it_works", "dashboards"): that page.
        Example: read_help(page="deployments").

page.description: Help page id, e.g. how_it_works, dashboards, deployments, protocols. Empty lists the pages.
page.title: Page

tools.name: list_node_types
tools.description:
Search the available computational nodes by task, name, or category. Results are
        paginated (limit 1 to 100, offset starting at 0); follow next_offset when has_more is true.
        Search for "fft", "smooth a noisy signal", or a protocol name to check actual availability.
        Example: list_node_types(search="websocket") or list_node_types(search="smooth a noisy signal", limit=10).

search.description: Words to search for in names, purposes and categories, e.g. fft, smooth a noisy signal, modbus.
search.title: Search

category.description: Only node types of this category (as list_node_types reports it). Empty for all.
category.title: Category

offset.description: Index of the first result; use next_offset from the previous page.
offset.title: Offset

tools.name: describe_node_type
tools.description:
Everything about one node type: its help page (purpose, typical uses, inputs and outputs,
        settings, tips and pitfalls, nodes it works well with), its pins, its settings with their
        defaults, and its ui settings. "settings_reference" says what every saved setting means
        (e.g. which number is which direction or operation). Read the help before using a node.
        Example: describe_node_type(node_type="HttpNode").

node_type.description: The exact node type name from list_node_types, e.g. HttpNode or PlotNode.
node_type.title: Node Type

tools.name: describe_theme_values
tools.description:
What a graph's look can set (see "Theme Studio" in get_guide): the themes, card materials and
        control families, and every value with its type and range. Filter by surface (Application,
        Node editor canvas, Nodes, Connections, Dashboard, Cards, Widgets) or group (Colors, Background, Edges,
        Glow, Shadows).
        Example: describe_theme_values(surface="Cards", group="Glow").

surface.description: Only values of this surface: Application, Node editor canvas, Nodes, Connections, Dashboard, Cards or Widgets. Empty for all.
surface.title: Surface

group.description: Only values of this group: Colors, Background, Edges, Glow or Shadows. Empty for all.
group.title: Group

tools.name: list_widget_styles
tools.description:
Discover native indicator/control style IDs, read-only vs interactive
        semantics, saved UI setting keys and display modes. Reports
        coarse style-family appearance hints and configurable display-only
        engineering unit fields; no rendered previews or dimensional math.
        Use before create_graph when selecting premium radar, analog/VU
        meters, LED, rotary knob or slider materials. Pages max 100 results.
        Example: list_widget_styles(kind="indicator_dial", gpu_only=true).

kind.description: Only styles of this kind: indicator_dial, indicator_horizontal, indicator_vertical, indicator_led, control_knob, control_slider_horizontal, control_slider_vertical, control_button, control_switch, hydraulic_indicator or hydraulic_control. Empty for all.
kind.title: Kind

family.description: Only styles of this material family, e.g. Aviation, Classic, Futuristic, Glass. Empty for all.
family.title: Family

search.description: Words to search for in style ids and names.
search.title: Search

gpu_only.description: Only the GPU shader-rendered premium styles.
gpu_only.title: Gpu Only

tools.name: describe_widget_style
tools.description:
Look up one exact stable style ID including its node UI key,
        read-only/control semantics, material family, unit presentation,
        GPU support and non-rendered appearance hints.
        Example: describe_widget_style(style_id="dial.aviation").

style_id.description: The exact style id from list_widget_styles, e.g. dial.aviation.
style_id.title: Style Id

tools.name: create_graph
tools.description:
Builds a .lazy file from a spec (see get_guide) and checks it. When ok is true it returns a
        download link for the user (on a hosted server) or saves it as save_as (on a local server);
        include_file also returns the whole file. Otherwise it returns the errors to fix.
        Example: create_graph(spec={"name": "Sine", "nodes": [{"id": "wave", "type": "FormulaGeneratorNode"}, {"id": "plot", "type": "PlotNode"}], "links": [{"from": "wave.out", "to": "plot.in"}]}).

spec.description: The graph spec: name, nodes, links, and optionally notes, dashboard and style (see get_guide).
spec.title: Spec

save_as.description: File name for the graph; on a local server it is saved under this name.
save_as.title: Save As

include_file.description: Also return the whole .lazy file in the answer.
include_file.title: Include File

tools.name: validate_graph
tools.description:
Checks a .lazy file (its JSON text, or a download link from create_graph) the way LazyAnalysis reads it.
        Example: validate_graph(graph_file=<the download link from create_graph>).

graph_file.description: The .lazy file: its JSON text, or a download link returned by create_graph.
graph_file.title: Graph File

tools.name: graph_to_spec
tools.description:
Turns a .lazy file (its JSON text, or a download link from create_graph) into a spec,
        to change it and build it again with create_graph.
        Example: graph_to_spec(graph_file=<the .lazy JSON text>), change the spec, then create_graph.

graph_file.description: The .lazy file: its JSON text, or a download link returned by create_graph.
graph_file.title: Graph File
